newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end up but off highs.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end up but off highs.

text.p: Singapore shares ended firmer but off their highs on Thursday on moderately light volume.
Dealers said buying was selective with some light bargain hunting see in blue chips.
"The market is actually not that strong. Most stocks came off their highs in the afternoon except for Cycle & Carriage which is propping up the index," said a dealer with a local brokerage.
Index linked stocks Cycle & Carriage rose 30 cents to close at S$17 with 353,000 units traded. This pulled the Straits Times Industrial index higher by 3.57 points to end at 2,199.35.
Total volume was 96.37 million with 178 gainers against 132 losers.

Malaysia's Berjaya Group topped the actives with more than 14 million traded and ended six cents higher at S$1.10. Dealers said the group turned in good results recently and would be reaping substantial profit from its sale of Berjaya Industrial.

Wong's Circuits closed 4.5 cents higher at US$1.03 on active volume of 4.86 million. Dealers said some funds are accumulating the printed circuit board maker. Gainers included DBS Land, OCBC foreign and Singapore Press foreign, while Fraser & Neave and UOB foreign were lower. - Doreen Siow 65-8703080 REUTER
